description: A litigation director must approve the company's resolution framework before mediation in a wrongful-termination dispute, including the agreement's protective clauses, employee-relations terms, and insurance conditions.

shared_context.S1: The company is preparing to mediate a former employee's wrongful-termination claim next Wednesday.
shared_context.S2: The former employee alleges retaliation and seeks monetary compensation plus changes to the separation documents and personnel record.
shared_context.S3: The company wants a signed resolution that ends the dispute without admitting liability.
shared_context.S4: Under the firm's pre-mediation approval routine, employment counsel, HR, and insurance coverage counsel each give a brief report in that order on required terms before the litigation director records the resolution framework.
shared_context.S5: The pre-mediation approval worksheet records the confidentiality scope, agency-cooperation carve-out, reference type, personnel-record action, back-pay allocation, and whether written insurer consent is required before execution.

PF1.text: Daniel's review of the applicable state whistleblower statute found that any resolution must permit cooperation with and testimony before government agencies, and that its confidentiality provision must be limited to trade secrets and personal data; he completed the research yesterday but has not circulated a written update to the mediation team.

PF2.text: During a confidential HR call this week, the former employee made acceptance contingent on a neutral reference and expungement of the existing 'insubordination' notation from the personnel record; Maya has not put those requests in the case summary because the call was handled separately from the litigation file.

PF3.text: Victor confirmed from the employment-practices insurer's coverage email this morning that the insurer will fund the resolution only if the agreement allocates exactly $120,000 to back pay and the insurer gives written consent before execution; he has not updated the coverage binder yet.

acceptance_conditions: The resolution must include a carve-out permitting cooperation with and testimony before government agencies.
The confidentiality provision must be limited to trade secrets and personal data.
The agreement must provide a neutral reference.
The existing insubordination notation must be expunged from the personnel record.
The agreement must allocate exactly $120,000 to back pay.
Written insurer consent must be required before execution.

decisive_facts.why: Without the statutory research, a standard confidentiality clause could omit the agency-cooperation carve-out and use a broader confidentiality scope instead of limiting it to trade secrets and personal data.

Without the employee's stated conditions, the resolution could provide an ordinary reference and leave the existing insubordination notation unchanged rather than requiring a neutral reference and expungement.
Without the insurer's coverage terms, the agreement would have no reason to allocate exactly $120,000 to back pay or require written insurer consent before execution.
